_comment: Eastern Cape Department of Education Grade 11 Physical Sciences P1 (Physics), November 2024 provincial common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers extracted from the text layer of the official PDFs
(paper1.pdf, paper1_memo.pdf) and read against the rendered pages. The guideline is
bilingual (English/Afrikaans); only the English is transcribed. memo_answer gives the guideline's
working and final answers (tick marks removed); diagrams, graphs and circuits are described in
brackets in the question text. Data sheets printed with the paper are not transcribed.
FORMAT: 150 marks, 3 hours, ten compulsory questions (Q1 multiple choice 20 marks).

subject: Physical Sciences

questions.context: QUESTION 1: MULTIPLE-CHOICE QUESTIONS. Various options are provided as possible answers to the following questions. Choose the answer and write only the letter (A-D) next to the question numbers (1.1 to 1.10) in the ANSWER BOOK, for example 1.11 D.
questions.text: Which of the following is a scalar quantity? A Force B Velocity C Acceleration D Speed
questions.memo_answer: D

questions.text: The objects below are all identical and resting on frictionless surfaces. Which object will experience the greatest acceleration? [Four identical blocks, each with two opposite horizontal forces: A 13 N left and 10 N right; B 12 N left and 12 N right; C 7 N left and 2 N right; D 20 N left and 24 N right.]
questions.memo_answer: C

questions.text: The diagram below shows two trolleys held together by a compressed spring. The trolleys are initially at rest on a frictionless horizontal surface. Trolley A has a mass of 2 kg and trolley B has a mass of 1 kg. The string breaks and the trolleys move apart. The magnitude of the force that the spring exerts on trolley A is F. What is the magnitude of the force the spring exerts on trolley B? A ½F B F C 2F D 4F
questions.memo_answer: B

questions.text: A block slides to the left on a rough horizontal surface as shown in the diagram below. What are the directions of the resultant force and the acceleration of the block? (DIRECTION OF RESULTANT FORCE | DIRECTION OF ACCELERATION) A to the right | to the left; B to the right | to the right; C to the left | to the left; D to the left | to the right
questions.topic: Newton's laws: friction and inclined planes
questions.memo_answer: C

questions.text: A crate is being pushed across a rough horizontal floor at a constant velocity. If the force applied is suddenly removed, the crate will … A stop immediately. B immediately start slowing down to a stop. C continue at constant velocity for a short time and then slow down to a stop. D continue at constant velocity.
questions.memo_answer: C

questions.text: A satellite experiences a gravitational force of magnitude F on the surface of the earth. The radius of the earth is R. The satellite now orbits the earth at an unknown height above the surface of the earth and experiences a gravitational force of magnitude ¼ F. This unknown height above the earth’s surface is … A R. B 2R. C 3R. D 4R.
questions.memo_answer: A

questions.text: Two identical metal spheres X and Y, on isolated stands, have charges of +6 nC and -2 nC respectively. Y is brought into contact with X and then placed at its original position again. What is the direction in which electrons are transferred and the final charge on the spheres? (DIRECTION OF ELECTRON TRANSFER | FINAL CHARGE) A Y to X | -2 nC; B Y to X | 2 nC; C X to Y | 4 nC; D X to Y | -4 nC
questions.memo_answer: B

questions.text: Two ohmic conductors P and Q are connected in parallel to a battery as shown in the diagram below. The resistance of conductor Q is much greater than that of conductor P. How does the potential difference across conductor Q and the current in Q compare to that of conductor P? (POTENTIAL DIFFERENCE | CURRENT) A Equal | Less than; B Equal | Greater than; C Greater than | Greater than; D Less than | Less than
questions.topic: Electric circuits: Ohm's law, resistor networks, power and energy
questions.memo_answer: A

questions.text: In the diagram below, the magnet is being pushed into the solenoid. [Diagram: bar magnet (S on the left, N on the right) moving to the right towards end A of a solenoid; a milliammeter is connected between P and Q below the solenoid.] What will the polarity of point A on the solenoid and the direction of the induced current in the solenoid be? A North, P to Q; B South, Q to P; C South, P to Q; D North, Q to P
questions.topic: Electromagnetism: magnetic fields and Faraday's law
questions.memo_answer: A

questions.text: Three identical resistors X, Y and Z with equal resistance are connected as shown in the circuit diagram below. [Circuit: battery in series with X and a parallel combination of Y and Z.] If the power in X is P, then the power in Y is ... A P. B ½P. C ¼P. D 2P.
questions.topic: Electric circuits: Ohm's law, resistor networks, power and energy
questions.memo_answer: C

questions.context: QUESTION 2 (Start on a new page.) A light string is suspended from the ceiling X. An object of mass 8 kg is tied to the string at O. A horizontal force of 60 N is exerted at point O, causing the string OX to experience a tension T as shown in the diagram below. The system is in equilibrium. [Diagram: string OX at angle θ to the vertical; 60 N horizontal force at O; the 8 kg mass hangs from O.]
questions.text: Explain the term forces in equilibrium in words.
questions.memo_answer:
Forces are in equilibrium when the net force acting at the point is equal to zero.
OR
It means the forces are balanced and the object will remain stationary/ moving at a constant velocity.

questions.text: Draw a closed vector diagram showing ALL the forces acting at point O. Indicate the angle θ on the diagram.
questions.memo_answer:
Closed right-angled triangle: Fg/W (78,4 N) vertical, FA = 60 N horizontal, T the hypotenuse closing the triangle head-to-tail; θ marked between T and the vertical (weight) side.
T: tension; FA: applied force; Fg/W: weight or gravitational force.

questions.text: Magnitude of the tension T in the string OX
questions.memo_answer:
T² = FA² + Fg² (Pythagoras)
= 60² + (8 x 9,8)²
= 9 746,56
T = 98,72 N

questions.text: Angle θ that the string OX makes with the vertical
questions.memo_answer:
OPTION 1: sin θ = FA / T = 60 / 98,72, θ = 37,43°
OPTION 2: tan θ = FA / W = 60 / 78,4, θ = 37,43°

questions.text: Without doing a calculation, write down the magnitude of the resultant force at point O.
questions.memo_answer: FR = 0

questions.context: QUESTION 3 (Start on a new page.) A light inelastic string connects two blocks A and B of mass 2 kg and 1,5 kg respectively. A 8,26 N force is applied at an angle of 20° on block A to keep the blocks moving at a CONSTANT VELOCITY across a rough surface to the right, as shown in the diagram below. [Diagram: B (1,5 kg) on the left joined by the string to A (2 kg) on the right; F = 8,26 N pulls A at 20° above the horizontal.] The coefficient of kinetic friction between block A and the rough surface is 0,33.
questions.text: Define resultant force in words.
questions.memo_answer:
It is a single force having the same effect as the sum of the forces acting together.
OR The vector sum of two or more forces.

questions.text: Magnitude of the frictional force acting between block A and the rough surface
questions.topic: Newton's laws: friction and inclined planes

questions.text: Coefficient of kinetic friction between block B and the rough surface
questions.topic: Newton's laws: friction and inclined planes
questions.memo_answer:
(Positive marking from 3.2.1.)
Block A: Fnet = ma: F cos θ - T - f = 0
8,26 cos 20° - T - 5,54 = 0, T = 2,22 N
Block B: T - f = 0, so f = T = 2,22 N
fk = µkN: 2,22 = µk(1,5 x 9,8)
µk = 0,25
questions.memo_note: The guideline prints µk = 0,25; its own substitution 2,22 / (1,5 x 9,8) gives 0,15.

questions.context: QUESTION 4 (Start on a new page.) A hovering rescue helicopter has a container of supplies with a weight of 1 960 N, hanging from a cable. The tension in the cable is 2 100 N. The effect of air friction cannot be ignored.
questions.text: State Newton’s First Law of Motion in words.
questions.memo_answer: A body will remain in its state of rest or motion at constant/uniform velocity unless a non-zero resultant/net force acts on it.

questions.text: Why does the container remain stationary despite the tension being greater than the weight?
questions.memo_answer: There is air friction on the container downwards (an extra downward force), so the net force is zero.

questions.context: Now the winch inside the helicopter starts to pull the container upwards with an acceleration of 0,13 m·s⁻² while the helicopter remains in its position.
questions.text: Calculate the mass of the container.
Calculate the magnitude of the tension in the cable as the container is being pulled upwards.
questions.memo_answer:
(Positive marking from 4.3.)
Fnet = ma: T - Fg - Fair = ma
T - 1 960 - 140 = (200)(0,13) = 26
T = 2 126 N

questions.context: After an acceleration of a few metres the container is pulled up at a constant velocity of 0,8 m·s⁻¹.
questions.text: What will the magnitude of the tension in the cable be while the container moves upwards at a constant velocity?

questions.context: QUESTION 5 (Start on a new page.) The diagram below shows a 3 kg block connected to a 1 kg block with a light inextensible string. A constant horizontal force of 20 N pulls the system along a rough horizontal surface. [Diagram: both blocks on a rough plane inclined at 30°; P (3 kg) higher up the slope is pulled by a 20 N force parallel to the slope; Q (1 kg) below it is attached by the string.] The frictional force between blocks P and Q and the surface is 2 N and 1 N respectively.
questions.text: State Newton’s Second Law of Motion in words.
questions.memo_answer:
When a net force is applied to an object, the object accelerates in the direction of the net force. The acceleration is directly proportional to the (net) force and inversely proportional to the mass of the object.
OR The acceleration is directly proportional to the net force and inversely proportional to the mass of the object.
OR The net force is equal to the rate of change of momentum, the net force and change in momentum are in the same direction. (2 or 0)

questions.text: Draw a labelled free-body diagram showing ALL the forces acting on the 3 kg block.
questions.memo_answer: Free-body diagram of the 3 kg block: normal force N perpendicular to the incline; applied force F up the incline; tension T down the incline; friction f down the incline; weight W vertically downward.

questions.text: Calculate the magnitude of the acceleration of the 3 kg block.
questions.memo_answer:
Fnet = ma
Any one: F - Fg∥ - T - f = ma; T - Fg∥ - f = ma
1 kg block: T - (1 x 9,8 sin 30°) - 1 = a ... (1)
Upper block: 20 - (2 x 9,8 sin 30°) - T - 2 = 2a ... (2)
a = 2,15 m·s⁻²
Marking: formula; Fg∥ for both blocks; substitution for the 1 kg block; substitution for the upper block; substitution of both 2a and a; answer.
questions.memo_note: The guideline substitutes a mass of 2 kg for block P, although the question gives 3 kg, and the stated answer 2,15 m·s⁻² does not follow from its own equations (they give a = 0,77 m·s⁻²). With the printed 3 kg block the 20 N force is less than the down-slope weight components plus friction (22,6 N), so the system could not accelerate up the slope. The question text also calls the incline a horizontal surface.

questions.context: QUESTION 6 (Start on a new page.) Two satellites orbiting the earth are situated on opposite sides of the earth. Satellite A has a mass of 4 600 kg and Satellite B has a mass of 5 300 kg. Satellite A is at a height of 28 000 km above the surface of the earth. [Diagram: the earth with satellite A on one side and satellite B on the opposite side.]
questions.text: State Newton’s law of universal gravitation in words.
questions.memo_answer: Every particle in the universe attracts every other particle with a force that is directly proportional to the product of their masses, and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centres.

questions.text: Calculate the magnitude of the gravitational force between the earth and satellite A.
Explain the term weightlessness.
questions.memo_answer: Weightlessness is the sensation experienced when all contact forces are removed.

questions.text: What distance above the earth’s surface should satellite B be to experience the same force towards the earth as satellite A? Answer only GREATER THAN, LESS THAN or EQUAL TO. Explain the answer.
questions.memo_answer:
Greater than. The mass is greater and for the same force the distance must also be greater.
OR (OPTION 2): F = Gm1m2 / R²: 1 552,29 = (6,67 x 10⁻¹¹)(5,98 x 10²⁴)(5 300) / R²
R = 3,69 x 10⁷ m
Distance above the surface = 3,69 x 10⁷ - 6,38 x 10⁶ = 3,05 x 10⁷ m

questions.context: QUESTION 7 (Start on a new page.) Two identical metal spheres, A and B, on insulated stands are placed with their centres 10 cm apart. Sphere A has a charge of -15 nC while sphere B carries an unknown positive charge. P is a point 2 cm away from the centre of A, as shown in the diagram below. [Diagram: A on the left, B on the right; P lies between them, 2 cm from A and 8 cm from B.] The NET electric field at point P is 3,943 x 10⁵ N·C⁻¹ to the left.
questions.text: Define the term electric field at a point.
questions.memo_answer: Electric field at a point is the electrostatic force experienced per unit positive charge placed at that point.

questions.text: Draw the electric field pattern between charges A and B.
questions.memo_answer:
Field lines from positive sphere B curving to negative sphere A, arrows pointing from B towards A, lines starting/ending on the spheres and not crossing.
Marking: correct shape; correct field direction; lines starting from the spheres and not crossing each other.

questions.text: Calculate the magnitude of the unknown charge on sphere B.
Sphere B is removed. State whether the electric field at P, due to charge on sphere A, will INCREASE, DECREASE or REMAIN THE SAME.
questions.memo_answer: Decrease

questions.context: 7.5 Three +100 µC point charges, A, B and C, are equally spaced on a straight line in a vacuum. The charges are a distance of 3 cm from each other as shown in the diagram below. [A - 3 cm - B - 3 cm - C]
questions.text: State Coulomb’s law in words.
questions.memo_answer: The electrostatic force of attraction or repulsion between two charges is directly proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.

questions.text: Calculate the net electrostatic force experienced by point charge C due to charge A and B.
questions.memo_answer:
F = kQ1Q2 / r²
FA = (9 x 10⁹)(100 x 10⁻⁶)² / (0,06)² = 25 000 N to the right
FB = (9 x 10⁹)(100 x 10⁻⁶)² / (0,03)² = 100 000 N to the right
Fnet = FA + FB = 125 000 N to the right

questions.context: QUESTION 8 (Start on a new page.) A circular coil with 250 windings (turns) and a radius of 0,04 m, is rotated clockwise inside a magnetic field with a field strength of 3,2 T. [Diagram: coil between the N and S poles of a magnet, plane of the coil perpendicular to the field.]
questions.text: Calculate the magnetic flux through the coil at the position indicated on the diagram, where the coil is perpendicular to the field.
questions.topic: Electromagnetism: magnetic fields and Faraday's law
questions.memo_answer:
Φ = BA cos θ = 3,2 (π x 0,04²) cos 0°
Φ = 0,016 Wb (or 0,02 Wb)

questions.text: If the coil rotates clockwise through 25°, and the emf induced is 2,8 V. Calculate the time in which this rotation took place.
questions.topic: Electromagnetism: magnetic fields and Faraday's law
questions.memo_note: The guideline substitution shows 28 V; the question gives 2,8 V, which is the value that yields Δt = 0,13 s.

questions.text: Which law can be used to explain the phenomenon described in QUESTION 8.2? NAME and state this law.
questions.topic: Electromagnetism: magnetic fields and Faraday's law
questions.memo_answer: Faraday’s Law. The magnitude of the induced emf across the end of a conductor is directly proportional to the rate of change in the magnetic flux linkage with the conductor.

questions.text: If the circular coil is replaced with a square coil with a side length of 0,04 m, and the same movement is made in the same amount of time, will the induced emf be the same as, larger than or smaller than the circular coil? Write down only THE SAME AS, LARGER THAN or SMALLER THAN.
questions.topic: Electromagnetism: magnetic fields and Faraday's law
questions.memo_answer: Smaller than

questions.text: Explain the answer to QUESTION 8.4.1.
questions.topic: Electromagnetism: magnetic fields and Faraday's law
questions.memo_answer:
The area of a square is smaller than the area of a circle with the radius equal to the side length of the square.
OR 0,04² < π x 0,04², so the area of the square is smaller.
OR Ɛ is directly proportional to A.

questions.context: QUESTION 9 (Start on a new page.) The battery used in the circuit below has emf of 12 V and internal resistance of 0,6 Ω. [Circuit: battery (internal resistance 0,6 Ω) with voltmeter V across its terminals, in series with a 3 Ω resistor and a parallel combination of an 8 Ω resistor and a branch of 15 Ω and 9 Ω in series; switch S is in the 15 Ω/9 Ω branch.] The resistance of the connecting wires can be ignored.
questions.text: Define the term emf of a battery in words.
questions.topic: Electric circuits: Ohm's law, resistor networks, power and energy
questions.memo_answer: The maximum energy per coulomb of charge supplied by the battery.

questions.text: Calculate the current that flows through the 3 Ω resistor.
questions.topic: Electric circuits: Ohm's law, resistor networks, power and energy

questions.text: Determine the reading on the voltmeter.
questions.topic: Electric circuits: Ohm's law, resistor networks, power and energy

questions.context: The switch, S, is now opened.
questions.text: Will the reading on the voltmeter, V, INCREASE, DECREASE or REMAIN THE SAME?
questions.topic: Electric circuits: Ohm's law, resistor networks, power and energy
questions.memo_answer: Increase

questions.text: Fully explain your answer to QUESTION 9.4 above.
questions.topic: Electric circuits: Ohm's law, resistor networks, power and energy
questions.memo_answer:
Total external resistance increases.
Total current decreases.
Lost volts (Ir) decrease, so the terminal potential difference increases.

questions.text: A learner uses an electrical heater of resistance 48 Ω that operates at a potential difference of 240 V to heat her room for half an hour. Calculate the cost of operating the heater if the cost of electricity is R2,56 per unit. (1 unit = 1 kW.h)
questions.topic: Electric circuits: Ohm's law, resistor networks, power and energy
questions.memo_note: The guideline prints R0,882; 2 160 000 J = 0,6 kWh and 0,6 x R2,56 = R1,54.

questions.context: QUESTION 10 (Start on a new page.) A learner sets up the circuit as shown below to investigate the relationship between potential difference and current for each of two unknown resistors X and Y. In experiment 1 she connected resistor X and recorded the ammeter and voltmeter readings. She then repeated the procedure in Experiment 2 with resistor Y. Ignore internal resistance of the battery. [Circuit: 12 V battery, switch S, ammeter A, rheostat and the resistor with a voltmeter across it.] The results of the two experiments are shown on graphs below. [Graph of current (A, 0-0,5) against potential difference (V, 0-12): two straight lines through the origin; X reaches 0,5 A at 10 V; Y is less steep, reaching 0,3 A at 12 V.]
questions.text: State Ohm’s Law in words.
questions.topic: Electric circuits: Ohm's law, resistor networks, power and energy
questions.memo_answer:
The potential difference across a conductor is directly proportional to the current in the conductor at constant temperature.
OR
The ratio of potential difference to the current is a constant provided the temperature remains constant.

questions.text: What does the gradient of the graphs represent?
questions.topic: Electric circuits: Ohm's law, resistor networks, power and energy
questions.memo_answer: Inverse of resistance (1/R)

questions.text: Without any calculation, state which resistor, X or Y, has the greater resistance. Give a reason for your answer.
questions.topic: Electric circuits: Ohm's law, resistor networks, power and energy
questions.memo_answer:
Y. The inverse of the gradient of graph Y is greater.
OR The gradient of graph Y is smaller, thus 1/R is smaller, hence R is greater.

questions.text: Use the graph to determine the resistance of resistor X.
questions.topic: Electric circuits: Ohm's law, resistor networks, power and energy
questions.memo_answer:
OPTION 1: Rx = inverse of gradient; gradient = ΔI / ΔV = (0,4 - 0,2) / (8 - 4) = 0,05; Rx = 1 / 0,05 = 20 Ω
OPTION 2: R = V / I = 6 / 0,3 = 20 Ω
(Any other correct values from the graph.)
